spec_references: Module-level declarations: "Function definition" supports "required-params" in the signature.
Subset restrictions → Import declarations lists `ballerina/lang.decimal` with `fromString`.
reason: The source declares an empty public main function with one required decimal parameter. Its only tested behavior is rejection of the command-line argument 0X1EF.A2P-2, supplied by the @args comment, with an expected panic. Function definitions and required parameters are supported, but the supplied specification does not cover executable entry-point argument binding, command-line decimal parsing, or the failure behavior of invalid command-line arguments. Support for numeric literals and decimal:fromString does not establish support for this separate invocation mechanism. Consequently the whole case depends on a not-covered feature, despite its ordinary function syntax.
unsupported_constructs: Command-line conversion to a decimal main parameter and rejection/panic behavior for invalid input.
test_design_notes: The hexadecimal-looking input is comment data, not a Ballerina numeric literal or deliberately malformed source syntax.
The @panic marker is on the main declaration; the empty function body contains no panic statement. No obvious migration defect is established from these two files.
